newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile economy slowdown won't extend into 97 - Aninat.
newsitem.headline: Chile economy slowdown won't extend into 97 - Aninat.

text.p: The slowing of the Chilean economy and high interest rates will not continue into next year, although lower commodity prices, especially for copper, could still prove to be a problem, said Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat.
"Unlike a part of 1995 and the whole of 1996 which have been a period of adjustment, 1997 will not be a year of adjustment," Aninat told reporters.
The Central Bank jacked up interest rates last year to cool the economy which had appeared in danger of overheating, making the authorities hard-pressed to meet their inflation targets.
The slowing in the economy due and restrictive monetary policy is known locally as "ajuste," or adjustment.
Aninat said the slide in the price of copper -- Chile's top export -- is likely to continue to cause difficulties, although the prices of other commodities look set to improve.
"Although there are some problems in international prices, especially in copper and oil, prices of other products are starting to show an improvement," he said.
Copper accounts for 40 percent of Chile's exports, with other key commodity exports including wood pulp and fishmeal.
